title: Amazon Linux 2 2017.12 - ALAS2-2026-4077: medium priority package update for perl-DBI
description:
Package updates are available for Amazon Linux 2 that fix the following vulnerabilities:
CVE-2026-88816:
	Fix FetchHashKeyName   on IV/NV

NOTE: Fixed by: https://github.com/perl5-dbi/dbi/commit/70962570212dc60a5428098cf2a0462ad5945851

CVE-2026-88815:
	Fix DBI::sql_type_cast on IV/NV

NOTE: Fixed by: https://github.com/perl5-dbi/dbi/commit/e5ad87e5602da995d28b4d65df222368b58d6702

CVE-2026-111879:
	DBI versions before 1.656 for Perl hang on a later open of a DBD::DBM table because a failed open_data does not release the table's lock. open_data creates the table's lock file and takes an exclusive flock on it for a CREATE, before the checks that can croak: a dbm_mldbm value that is not a module name, a failing tie, or a missing data file. The croak unwinds before the table object is blessed, so nothing releases the lock, and the meta data holding the open descriptor stays cached on the database handle. The dbm_mldbm and dbm_type values come from the DSN or the connect attributes, so a caller that chooses the serializer or the storage backend can trigger the failure. The flock has no timeout, so a later open of that table (even through a separate database handle) blocks for as long as the handle holding the stale lock lives, in the same process or any other.

CVE-2026-108518:
	DBI versions before 1.656 for Perl crash via type confusion in dbi_profile when a database handle is destroyed under a Profile Path with an {attr} element. An {attr} element names a database handle attribute, which dbi_profile reads from the handle's inner hash. It expects the inner handle as a reference and dereferences it, but a handle that is being destroyed hands back the inner hash itself, so the dereference yields the hash's bucket array. A type check on that pointer usually fails and the call goes unprofiled. When the memory it addresses passes the check, the attribute lookup dereferences a NULL or invalid pointer and the process dies on SIGSEGV. The Path is set by the application, by the Profile handle attribute, or by the DBI_PROFILE environment variable, so `DBI_PROFILE={ImplementorClass}` can crash an unmodified program.
